title: Novus Retail — Billing export & route-finance dry run
topics: Latency vs cost tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated)
summary: AE + SE walked Novus through Redwood Console focusing on per-route telemetry, how to attribute cost to product routes, and how billing exports map to chargeback. Customer raised questions about dedicated GPU pools, VPC KMS integration, and sample billing CSV layout. Agreed next steps: share security pack, pricing spreadsheet, and a one-week pilot with traffic replay + billing export.
next_steps: Redwood to send security docs + SOC2 artifacts by 2026-07-16
Share sample billing export and mapping sheet by 2026-07-16
Schedule pilot kickoff (traffic replay) w/ SE on 2026-07-20
Provide Dedicated capacity estimate and month-to-month pricing by 2026-07-17
action_items: Alex Moore: Email pricing sheet and tiered cost models (due 2026-07-17)
Priya Shah: Prepare pilot runbook + sample billing export mapping (due 2026-07-16)
Ravi Anand (Novus): Share 24h sample traffic trace to replay (due 2026-07-18)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14 11:00 PT / 14:00 ET
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moore (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Sam Li (Novus Head of ML), Jordan Park (CTO), Erica Gomez (Finance), Ravi Anand (SRE)

[00:00] Alex Moore: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro — I'm Alex, AE, Priya is our solutions engineer, Daniel will help with pilot ops. how are you all?
[00:09] Sam Li: good, thanks. excited to see how the console can help our cost allocation — Erica is, uh, especially interested in the billing output.
[00:16] Erica Gomez: yep, we need something our finance team can import into our chargeback system, CSV ideally.
[00:22] Priya Shah: absolutely, we'll walk through the per-route dashboard and the billing export. quick note — some transcript may have small auto-caption quirks, sorry if you see K-V cash instead of KV cache, that kind of thing.
[00:34] Jordan Park: lol, yeah. as long as the numbers line up.
[00:38] Priya Shah: alright jumping in — opening the Console, first view is the usage overview. you can see token volume, embeddings, and per-route breakdown. so this route here, "product-search", you can slice by model, region, and time window.
[01:02] Sam Li: is that per-request attribution or per-token?
[01:05] Priya Shah: good q, it's per-token cost attribution — we normalize compute against tokens and model profile. so you get a dollar-per-token metric and then we multiply by the tokens used by each route.
[01:16] Daniel Kim: to add, we also include overhead — like batching efficiency and cache hits — those appear as a separate column so finance can see effective unit cost.
[01:28] Ravi Anand: question, what if we run on Dedicated? do the per-token numbers change?
[01:33] Priya Shah: yes, the console supports both Hosted and Dedicated. for Dedicated we feed in committed capacity amortization — so the unit economics can show committed cost per token plus burst usage. you can model different commit tiers in the UI.
[01:47] Erica Gomez: can we export that modeled chargeback per month? I need line items that map to our GL codes.
[01:53] Priya Shah: yes — export formats include CSV and a JSON line-level export. the CSV has columns: date, route, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_cost, cache_savings, batch_efficiency_factor, total_cost, cost_center_tag. we demo that live next.
[02:12] Alex Moore: i'll flag — for the export, we'll include a sample mapping sheet that shows how the columns map to common GL fields.
[02:19] Sam Li: good. can you show how you tag routes? we have a mix of API endpoints and internal async jobs.
[02:25] Priya Shah: folders + route tags — you can assign a route to a product team or service. tags flow into the export, and we can auto-map to your chargeback keys via the mapping sheet.
[02:37] Jordan Park: security question — we need KMS integration and to keep keys in our cloud. SOC2 and the audit logs are must-haves.
[02:45] Priya Shah: absolutely. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and integrates with AWS KMS and GCP KMS. audit logs are available for every request; we can retain logs per your retention policy in Private. for Hosted, we provide SOC2 reports and detailed request logs but keys are managed by Redwood.
[03:05] Jordan Park: how about SSO? we use Okta with SAML and SCIM for user provisioning.
[03:10] Alex Moore: SSO with SAML is supported, SCIM provisioning as well. we'll include the SSO config guide in the packet.
[03:18] Ravi Anand: latency is a concern — some routes are latency-sensitive P0 customer-facing search, others are async batch. what recommendations do you have?
[03:26] Priya Shah: for the P0 routes, we recommend pinning to a low-latency model variant and enabling prefix KV caching; set a smaller batching window to keep latency tight. for batch jobs you can route to a lower-cost quantized model and larger batch windows. the Console lets you create routing policies by route.
[03:44] Sam Li: how big is the latency hit with aggressive quantization? we need quality checks.
[03:48] Priya Shah: depends on the model and quantization level; typically INT8 gives minor quality drift for retrieval-augmented responses, but for generation it can be more visible. Redwood Optimize can run evals against your prompt sets to surface regression risk.
[04:04] Daniel Kim: we can set up a canary: route 5% to the quantized variant and compare rouge/bleu or business metrics. the Console will show quality regressions tied to prompts.
[04:15] Erica Gomez: you mentioned cost modeling — how do you show amortization? do we see monthly committed baseline split across routes?
[04:21] Priya Shah: yes — committed capacity is represented as a baseline in the Cost tab. you can allocate baseline across teams manually or by usage percentage. there's also a chargeback automation rule that will pro-rate reserved costs by route usage or by a fixed tag.
[04:36] Sam Li: great. show us a sample billing export please.
[04:40] Priya Shah: exporting now — downloading CSV... open it. you'll see sample rows: 2026-07-13, product-search, gptx-7b-quant, 1,200 in, 400 out, compute 32.40, cache savings 5.60, total 26.80, cost_center: retail-search.
[05:02] Erica Gomez: the numbers seem okay but we need currency in USD and exchange column for our offshore teams.
[05:08] Priya Shah: yes, currency and exchange columns can be toggled. also there's a currency normalization step if you want to bill internal teams in USD while costs are incurred in different clouds.
[05:19] Jordan Park: what's the typical sizing for Dedicated for an org our size — say peak 600 rps across model calls?
[05:26] Alex Moore: offhand, that usually sits around a 12-16 GPU fleet depending on seq length and model. we'll run a sizing calc once you share the traffic trace. Priya will follow up with estimated node count and costs.
[05:38] Ravi Anand: and is Dedicated month-to-month or annual only?
[05:41] Alex Moore: we offer both commits — monthly reserved and annual — monthly has a slightly higher rate but flexible. we'll include both numbers.
[05:48] Sam Li: are there built-in alerts for cost anomalies? we had a rogue loop once that spiked tokens.
[05:53] Priya Shah: yes, the Console has anomaly detection thresholds and can alert on sudden token growth, unusual route patterning, or per-route cost spikes. you can pipe alerts to Slack or PagerDuty.
[06:06] Daniel Kim: also worth noting I mentioned earlier, KV cache hit rate shows up as a 'savings' line — you can see where a bad prompt causes cache miss storms.
[06:16] Erica Gomez: if we run a pilot replay, will the billing export from the pilot mirror production? we need to prove chargeback works before going live.
[06:24] Priya Shah: yes the pilot will produce the same export shape. Pilot note: if you replay traffic into Redwood Dedicated or Hosted pilot, we time-stamp and label it so finance can separate it from production usage.
[06:37] Jordan Park: compliance again — can audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[06:41] Priya Shah: yes, we can forward logs via secure syslog or push to a GCS/S3 bucket that your SIEM ingests. for Private we can stream logs into your VPC directly.
[06:53] Sam Li: about routing policies — can they be dynamic? like route to cheaper model overnight?
[06:58] Priya Shah: yep, scheduling/rules exist. you can set time-of-day policies or performance triggers — e.g., use quantized at 1am-5am for batch jobs, switch to low-latency variant during business hours.
[07:12] Ravi Anand: is there rate-limiting per-route? we need guardrails to prevent runaway costs.
[07:16] Daniel Kim: per-route quotas and throttles are supported; you can set hard caps and soft alerts.
[07:22] Erica Gomez: earlier you mentioned model catalog — how are models labeled in exports — sometimes we have 3rd-party models and in-house ones.
[07:29] Priya Shah: each model_variant column includes vendor, model_name, quantization. e.g., "redwood/gptx-7b@int8" or "openai/gpt-4o@fp16" — if you add an in-house model artifact, we tag it as private and it appears with your account id.
[07:46] Jordan Park: any gotchas with tokenization differences across vendors? we use different tokenizers internally.
[07:51] Priya Shah: yes, token counts can vary by tokenizer, so we normalize using our token-profile for each model. we also include raw character counts if you prefer to reconcile with your internal metrics.
[08:03] Sam Li: what's the latency for fetching costs in the Console? is data near real-time?
[08:07] Priya Shah: usage is near real-time with a small aggregation window (1-5 minutes). billing exports are generated once per hour or on-demand for a custom range.
[08:17] Alex Moore: quick live demo of a routing change: switching "product-search" to quantized for the overnight schedule — update policy — commit — the Console shows projected savings and risk score.
[08:32] Sam Li: that risk score — is that from Redwood Optimize?
[08:35] Priya Shah: yes, Optimize runs offline evals on prompt sets you give it and assigns a risk score for quality regressions. we can surface examples of changed outputs.
[08:45] Erica Gomez: do you store prompt sets? any privacy concerns?
[08:48] Priya Shah: prompt sets can be uploaded and stored encrypted; for Private deployments everything remains in your VPC. for Hosted we can redact or hash prompts if required.
[08:58] Jordan Park: what about data residency — some of our EU customers must keep PII in EU regions. can we pin models and data regionally?
[09:05] Priya Shah: yes, region pinning is supported; requests can be routed to a region-specific deployment and exports will reflect region tags.
[09:15] Sam Li: okay, let's talk pilot — what does Redwood need from us?
[09:18] Priya Shah: ideally a 24-hour traffic trace plus expected seq lengths and sample prompts; define 2-3 routes to include: product-search (latency P0), pricing-chat (P1), nightly-summarize (batch). we'll replay traffic into a pilot environment and surface the billing export.
[09:34] Erica Gomez: timeline?
[09:36] Alex Moore: we proposed kickoff 2026-07-20 earlier — Priya will run the replay, then 3 business days of monitoring, then produce the export.
[09:46] Ravi Anand: if we find cost spikes, can we automatically fallback to a cheaper model?
[09:50] Daniel Kim: yes, routing fallback policies can fall back to a compatible model variant or route to a different region. we recommend a canary first.
[09:59] Jordan Park: any demo of chargeback dashboard visuals?
[10:02] Priya Shah: pulling up the chargeback view — shows team-level spend, route-level drift, and a waterfall of committed vs burst. you can toggle to view per-tag or group by service.
[10:14] Sam Li: can we automate internal billing invoices? export to our S3 and our ETL ingests it.
[10:18] Priya Shah: yes S3 drop + notification is standard. we'll give an example S3 prefix layout.
[10:24] Alex Moore: quick note — competitors sometimes only give top-level spend numbers; our differentiator is the route-level attribution and the ability to map to GL codes. that matters to finance teams.
[10:36] Erica Gomez: that's what i'm excited about.
[10:39] Priya Shah: last thing — I'll show the anomaly alert configuration for finance: set threshold at 2x baseline or absolute token delta and route will trigger a PagerDuty incident.
[10:50] Sam Li: ok, recap me on deliverables please.
[10:53] Alex Moore: sure — Alex to send pricing + sample billing export, Priya to share pilot runbook and mapping sheet, Redwood to provide SOC2 + security packet, Novus to share traffic trace and confirm finance contacts.
[11:06] Jordan Park: sounds good, thanks. any blockers on our side?
[11:09] Erica Gomez: none yet, will coordinate finance review after getting the sample export.
[11:16] Alex Moore: great, we'll follow up in email and calendar. thanks everyone.

End transcript.
